title: Out-of-town producers hear New Orleans bands; records are a canned experience
summary: Visitors from the West Coast warmed to the New Orleans sound in clubs, but one producer pointed out that record buyers lack the club ambience, so the record must stand alone.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Well, I'd get the opposite of that, for instance. You know, you'd get guys who'd come here maybe from the West Coast where they were used to hearing the bands out there play a certain way. And, and at first be a little put off by, by what they hear in New Orleans to, to, you could watch them and see them change.

You know the old thing. Right. You know, guys snapping their fingers up, moving them. You could actually see them get into it because New Orleans bands move people. You know, if I took a guy to a club and he listened, after a while, he, he, if he was sensitive at all, if he just let his hair down, he was into it, you know.

And, and, and so, so that was it. In fact, I have, I forget the guy's name now. One of them, I forget who it was, but one of, one of the guys said that he didn't want me taking him to clubs anymore. You want to bring the guys? Yeah. And, and, and he said, and I remember like it was yes. He says, look, he says, man, he says, with a, with a cool drink and a warm girl, they all sounded good. You know?
Yeah, right. You're going to take.

Yeah. In other words, and he had a, he had a point. And the point was that the people who bought, who bought the record weren't going to be in the ambience of a club, weren't, weren't going to be there with a, with a date or girlfriend,
du jour, or du soi, whatever you want to call it. People don't buy a live experience. They buy a canned experience on that record.

And it had to be, it had to be entirely in what they heard, since they weren't going to be seeing anything, hearing, and feeling any ambience, smelling any, whatever, you know. And, and, and, and he was correct, of course. So, so, so, so. I mean, who was?
